keyword: how to become a data scientist after 10th
title: How to Become a Data Scientist After 10th (2026)
desc: A year-by-year plan to become a data scientist after Class 10: maths and stream choices, Python, machine learning, projects, certificates and salary.
h1: How to become a data scientist after 10th
lead: A plan for a Class 10 student and their parent to read together. Every step comes from a real 624-hour, three-year data science curriculum, so you can see what a student actually learns and builds each year.
role_intro: A data scientist uses data to answer hard questions and make predictions. They clean messy data, test ideas with statistics, build machine learning models, and explain what the results mean for a business. The role sits between maths, code and clear communication.
in_short: Yes, you can start after Class 10. Python, SQL and statistics are taught from zero, so no coding background is needed.
Plan for about three years of skill building: data and statistics, then machine learning, then deep learning and generative AI.
Maths matters more here than in most tech roles. Keep Mathematics in Class 11 and 12 if you possibly can, because modelling rests on statistics and algebra.
start_answer: Yes. A student can start learning data science right after Class 10, because the first months teach computing, Python and basic statistics from the beginning, with no prior coding expected.
start_bridge: Your Class 11 and 12 stream matters a lot for this role, because data science leans on maths. Here is how each path looks.
streams: B.Tech through JEE Main, plus B.Sc in statistics, mathematics or computer science. The strongest base for modelling.

start_extra: If you are still deciding between a course and a career, our data science after 10th guide explains the course side. This page is about the role itself: what a data scientist does and how to get there step by step.
roadmap_answer: The roadmap runs over three years: year 1 builds Python, SQL, statistics and analysis, year 2 builds machine learning and data pipelines, and year 3 adds deep learning, NLP, generative AI and a portfolio.
year_focus: Year 1: learn to read data with Python, SQL and statistics
Year 2: build and test machine learning models on real data
Year 3: go deeper with deep learning, NLP and generative AI, then prove it
fit_note: This program goes further than many data science paths: it includes data engineering, MLOps and generative AI. It does not replace a mathematics degree. Students aiming at AI research roles usually also need a degree in mathematics, statistics or computer science.
skills_answer: A data scientist needs statistics, Python with NumPy and Pandas, SQL, data cleaning, machine learning, model evaluation, some data engineering, deep learning basics and the ability to explain results to people who are not technical.

certs_answer: Certificates such as IBM Data Science and Microsoft AI-300 can show an employer specific skills, but each one is awarded by its own body after its own assessment, and a portfolio of real models still counts most.

cert_notes.IBM Data Science Professional Certificat: A 12-course series on Coursera covering Python, SQL, data visualisation and machine learning. IBM says no prior experience is required, with high school maths helpful.
cert_notes.Microsoft AI-300 (Machine Learning Opera: An intermediate exam on running machine learning and generative AI systems on Azure. Microsoft expects a data science background with Python, so it sits in year 2 after the basics.

cert_extra: The roadmap also prepares for Microsoft DP-900 and the Google Data Analytics certificate in year 1, which suit the analysis side of the role.
notfor_answer: This path is not for you if you dislike maths, want instant results, or would rather build apps than question data, since much of a data scientist's day is checking whether an answer is really true.

salary_answer: Indicative ranges for data science roles in India are about ₹4 to 8 lakh a year for freshers, ₹10 to 22 lakh at 3 to 5 years, and ₹25 to 50 lakh or more for senior people.
faqs: How many years does it take to become a data scientist after 10th?

Plan for about three years of steady learning to build job-ready data science skills, such as the 3-year, 624-hour Data Science & AI program. Many employers also expect a degree, so the full route usually runs through Class 11 and 12 and a degree, with skills built alongside.
Can I become a data scientist without maths?

It is very hard. Data science rests on statistics, probability and algebra, and the program teaches statistics in two full modules. Without Mathematics in Class 11 and 12, analyst roles stay open, but you would need to relearn school maths for modelling.
What is the difference between a data scientist and a data analyst?

A data analyst mainly explains what happened, using SQL, statistics and dashboards. A data scientist also builds models that predict what will happen. In this roadmap, year 1 covers the analyst skills and years 2 and 3 add the data scientist skills.
Do I need to learn deep learning to become a data scientist?

Not for every job, since many data scientists work mostly with statistics and classic machine learning. The roadmap still covers deep learning, NLP and computer vision in year 3, because more data science work now involves text and images.
Does the program guarantee a data science job?
No. The program aims at job readiness through skills, monthly projects and a GitHub portfolio, but it does not guarantee a job, internship, salary or exam pass.
context_fact: Nasscom's Strategic Review 2026 describes AI moving from an optional extra to core infrastructure in India's tech industry. That is why this roadmap does not stop at analysis, and carries data science through to machine learning in production and generative AI.
